passage:
Wed, 11 pm
Did something today I keep thinking about.
Rukmini got picked as science fair lead instead of me. Instead of telling her I was hurt, I went to Farhan and Joel at lunch and said she only got it because she flatters Sir. Then I told Anita that Rukmini laughed at her project idea. (She didn't. Not really.)
By last period, Farhan and Anita weren't talking to Rukmini. I felt good for about an hour. Like I had a team.
Then I saw her eating alone by the water tap, and the good feeling went sour.
Why didn't I just say it to her face? Because if I said "I'm jealous", she might laugh, and then I'd have nobody. Easier to make everyone else angry for me.
Tomorrow: tell Anita the truth about the project thing. Maybe say sorry to Rukmini. Maybe.
Lokesh

qa.q: What role did Rukmini get instead of Lokesh?
qa.a: Rukmini got picked as science fair lead.

qa.q: How did Lokesh feel after seeing Rukmini eating alone?
qa.a: The good feeling of having a team went sour, and Lokesh felt guilty seeing what the stories had done.

qa.q: What could Lokesh have done at the moment of being passed over?
qa.a: Lokesh could have told Rukmini directly about feeling disappointed instead of recruiting Farhan and Anita against her; tomorrow's plan to tell Anita the truth is a good start.

qa.q: What was the day like for Rukmini?
qa.a: She likely felt confused and isolated, suddenly shut out by Farhan and Anita without knowing why, and ended up eating alone by the tap.

grounding: A student, hurt at being passed over, complains to Farhan, Joel and Anita and twists a story to gain allies instead of speaking to Rukmini directly.

passage:
Yash, you're telling me you told Neha what Rohan said about her so she'd be on your side? Sit. Let your Divyansh Mama tell you about the summer I was fifteen.
I had a fight with my best friend, Tony, over a cricket bat. Instead of talking to him, I went to our friend Salim. "Do you know what Tony said about you?" Half true, half stretched. Salim got angry. Then I went to Tony: "Salim's saying things about you." Soon the whole gang was split.
I felt clever. I had allies. I never had to sit across from Tony and say, "You hurt me."
By August, nobody trusted anybody. The three of us didn't speak for a year.
One day Salim asked me, straight: "Divyansh, did Tony ever actually say that?" I couldn't answer.
Talking to Tony would have taken ten minutes. The mess took a year.

qa.q: What was the fight between Divyansh and Tony about?
qa.a: A cricket bat.

qa.q: Why did young Divyansh carry stories between friends instead of talking to Tony?
qa.a: He was afraid that talking directly was risky, and he felt smug and clever having allies without facing Tony.

qa.q: At what point could Divyansh have stopped the mess?
qa.a: At the start, by sitting with Tony and saying "You hurt me," instead of carrying half-true messages to Salim.

qa.q: How might Salim have felt when he asked Divyansh directly?
qa.a: Salim probably felt suspicious and hurt, realising he may have been used in a fight that wasn't his.

grounding: An uncle recalls pulling a third friend into a quarrel with stretched messages to gain allies, because direct talk felt risky.

passage:
The school cricket selection was in one hour, and Imran was sitting with Binita on the bleachers while the rain made the pitch slippery and the coach waited for it to stop.
"You know Karan, right?" Imran said. "He told the coach I can't field. Behind my back." It wasn't exactly true. Karan had only said Imran dropped two catches in practice. "Can you tell the coach Karan's lazy? You're the scorer. He listens to you."
Binita looked at him. "Why don't you talk to Karan?"
"Because he'll argue."
"So you want me to be your shield."
Imran felt his face heat. She was right. Talking to Karan meant hearing things he didn't want to hear. Using Binita felt safer.
"Forget it," he said. "I'll talk to him."
The rain eased. He walked across to where Karan was stretching. "Hey. Did you tell the coach about the catches?"

qa.q: How long until the cricket selection?
qa.a: The selection was in one hour.

qa.q: How did Imran feel when Binita called herself his shield?
qa.a: Imran felt embarrassed and caught, realising he was using her because direct talk with Karan felt risky.

qa.q: Which choice did Imran make in the end, and why was it better?
qa.a: He went to talk to Karan directly, which avoids dragging Binita in and deals with the real issue.

qa.q: How does Binita see Imran's request?
qa.a: Binita sees it as being used as a shield in a fight that isn't hers, which is why she asks why he doesn't talk to Karan.

grounding: It shows a teenager trying to use a third person as a shield against a rival under time pressure, then choosing direct talk.

passage:
On the rooftop of their Chennai apartment block, Hrithik leaned on the water tank and said to Rekha, "Did you know Nisha thinks your dance at the annual day was boring? She said it at tuition."
Nisha hadn't said boring. She'd said "long." But Hrithik was annoyed with Nisha for sitting with the new boy, and he wanted Rekha on his side.
Rekha's face fell. "She said that?"
"Yeah. I just thought you should know."
Later, Rekha went quiet with Nisha. Nisha went quiet with Hrithik. By the weekend, the three of them, who had played on this roof since they were small, were sitting in separate corners.
Hrithik watched them and felt oddly empty. He had the ally he wanted. But he'd lost two friends, and he had never once told Nisha what actually bothered him.
On Monday he found Nisha at the gate. "I twisted what you said. I'm sorry. I was jealous about the new boy."

qa.q: What word did Nisha actually use about the dance?
qa.a: She'd said "long."

qa.q: Why did Hrithik twist Nisha's words?
qa.a: Hrithik felt jealous and annoyed that Nisha sat with the new boy, and wanted Rekha as an ally instead of facing Nisha directly.

qa.q: What did Hrithik do on Monday that helped?
qa.a: He went to Nisha directly, admitted he twisted her words, apologised, and named his jealousy.

qa.q: How did Rekha feel when Hrithik told her?
qa.a: Rekha felt hurt and let down, her face falling, believing a friend called her dance boring.

grounding: It shows a teenager carrying twisted messages to stir jealousy and gain an ally, because telling a friend directly felt risky.

passage:
"Hrithik, can I tell you something? But don't say I said it." Lalremsiami leaned on the lab counter.
"Okay..."
"Mawii told me she only sits with you because you help with maths."
Hrithik's pencil stopped. "She said that?"
"Kind of. Basically. I just think you should know who your real friends are."
"Why didn't you tell her it was mean?"
"I'm telling you, aren't I?"
Hrithik frowned. "You and Mawii fought yesterday, right? About the fest group?"
Lalremsiami felt her face heat. "That's not the point."
"Feels like it's the point. If you're angry with her, talk to her. Don't make me pick."
He went back to his diagram. Lalremsiami stared at her shoes. She had wanted him on her side so Mawii would feel alone the way she had yesterday. Hearing it out loud, it sounded small.
"Fine," she muttered. "I'll talk to her at lunch."

qa.q: What did Lalremsiami claim Mawii said?
qa.a: That Mawii only sits with Hrithik because he helps with maths.

qa.q: Why did Lalremsiami go to Hrithik instead of Mawii?
qa.a: Lalremsiami felt hurt and angry after yesterday's fight and wanted Mawii to feel alone too, so pulling Hrithik onto her side felt safer than talking directly.

qa.q: What did Hrithik do well?
qa.a: He noticed the fight behind the message, refused to pick a side, and pushed Lalremsiami to talk to Mawii herself.

qa.q: How might Mawii feel if Hrithik had believed the message?
qa.a: Mawii could have lost a friend without knowing why, feeling confused and shut out over words she may never have said.

grounding: Shows a teenager carrying a hurtful message to a third person to gain an ally after a fight, because direct talk felt risky.
